P1-2025JUN-Q46.passage:
Read the following passage and answer the questions:

A person who takes the trouble to form his own ideas and opinions will feel that he owes no responsibility to the majority opinion for his conclusions. If he is a genuine lover of truth, if he is moved by a desire to see things as they are and by an aversion to holding ideas that do not correspond with the facts, he will be wholly free of the approval of the people around him. When he proceeds to apply his opinions to the practical conduct of life, the position is different. There are then good reasons why his conduct should be less rigid. The society he lives in is an ancient and joint growth. The ideas and traditions of the people with whom he disagrees have not come about by mere chance.

These ideas and traditions all have their roots in a certain real, presumed fitness. They have, to a certain depth, a hold at the root on the lives of a part of the present generation. Their fitness to one another may by now have come to an end. That is only one side of the truth. The most zealous propaganda cannot pervade them. In common speech we refer to a generation as something in which all its parts and members, while being homogeneous, form a kind of true unity. Yet it is not merely that. It is a whole, but a whole in constant change, its factors and elements changing within. It is not one generation but many.
options: will praise the quality of the food.
will criticise what he does not like.
will be completely free of the approval of the people around him.
